entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How old is he, and how long has he led the Black Guard?
entries.answer: Other (write my own)
entries.custom_text: He has always been in the military. He had his daughter at 30. His daughter is now 20. He started the black guard from scratch and the main character is under the first black guard division ever created.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Which sin tempts him most (the bible says he is secretly very Proud)?
entries.answer: Other (write my own)
entries.custom_text: He looks humble and intelligent and smart and ambitious and humorous and just and caring and thinks what is best for the empire. Internally he is seeking the power that will save humanity and doesn’t believe the empire is doing it right. He was secretly born in a rival kingdom

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne

entries.answer: Against it — he wants to use corruption, not count it

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: His role toward Alaric and Seraphina?
entries.answer: Other (write my own)
entries.custom_text: He mentors and truly sees Alaric as the future, but he will have to slowly change Alaric’s views to better the world. Truly loves his daughter but humanity comes first

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Does Seraphina know Cassian was secretly born in a rival kingdom?

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What role does Seraphina's mother play?
entries.answer: She is Cassian's conscience. She is not aware of his secrets.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: He was secretly born in a rival kingdom. Which one?
entries.answer: A south-east kingdom still at war with the Southern Kingdoms.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What is the 'power that will save humanity' he is seeking?
entries.answer: He seeks a power tied to spirit-tech. He thinks it means a bargain with the fallen, but he doesn't fully know or understand who or what the fallen are.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What does Cassian offer the fallen?
entries.answer: He doesn't fully know or understand who or what the fallen are, only that there is a power tied to spirit-tech.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How does Cassian hope to use corruption?
entries.answer: To power spirit-tech.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: When does Alaric first notice Cassian quietly bending his views?
entries.answer: Alaric kind of falls into Cassian's ideology at first, but Seraphina talks it through with Alaric, and over time they both start to see something is off.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Who knows Cassian was secretly born in a rival kingdom?
entries.answer: Nobody alive.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What is the spirit-tech power Cassian is chasing?
entries.answer: All of the above: an ancient device that opens a crossing, powered by pulling energy out of corrupted things; the Flame Order forbade and hid it; Cassian doesn't know exactly what it is and follows rumors.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How does Cassian's wife act as his conscience?
entries.answer: Her faith keeps him tied to the Flame Order's teachings.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne

entries.answer: Dravenmoor (named by Story; Chumi may rename).

entries.question: How do ordinary people come in contact with the spirit world?
entries.answer: It is disputed: kingdoms and peoples are divided over the answer (crossings, faint presence everywhere, human choices, omens), and the disagreement itself divides them.

entries.question: Who rules the Empire?
entries.answer: An Emperor with a Council of High Lords.

entries.question: Why is it called the Black Guard?
entries.answer: Cassian named it when he founded it from scratch: black like the night.

entries.question: Where is Book 1's first command?
entries.answer: The Desert Kingdom border. (Only the location is canon; the 'silent frontier / missing patrols / blaming spirit-humanoids' setup is draft, not canon, and the link to Rashid's war is not decided.)

entries.question: What's going on at the Desert Kingdom border when Book 1's first command begins?
entries.answer: The Desert Kingdom is preparing for another push from the enemy. The enemy armies have 2 paths they could take to get to the desert kingdom capital.

entries.question: Who is the enemy pushing toward the desert kingdom capital?
entries.answer: Both the unconquered part of the desert kingdom and a rival kingdom beyond the desert.

entries.question: Who holds the desert kingdom's capital right now?
entries.answer: The Empire holds the desert kingdom's capital.

entries.question: What are the two paths the enemy could take to the desert kingdom capital?
entries.answer: Path 1: a large canyon with a large desert crossing, with one major city. Path 2: the main roads with many fortified cities (seems like the more obvious way).

entries.question: Where is the Black Guard sent?
entries.answer: Alaric's Banner goes to the canyon; the others go to the cities.

entries.question: Which path does the enemy actually take?
entries.answer: The enemy takes the canyon, straight into Alaric's Banner.

entries.question: Does Alaric's Banner know the enemy is coming their way?
entries.answer: After studying maps, technology, enemy habits and previous war conduct, Alaric sees something can very likely happen. The High Lord also sees something, but the other commanders don't see it or don't see it as likely. Other Black Guard Banners want to be where they will be the most help; some Banner commanders are noble and want glory, some just feel they need to be smart about it and be where the enemy will be.

entries.question: Which High Lord also sees the canyon attack coming?
entries.answer: Cassian will see it but likes how Alaric is choosing it. Rashid sees something but is overruled by his confident advisors and division commanders.

entries.question: Does Alaric's Banner face the canyon attack alone?
entries.answer: The canyon city has a division.

entries.question: Whose division is in the canyon city?
entries.answer: The general is a desert kingdom general. 3/4 of his division is desert kingdom regiments and the rest are Imperial regiments, which this general favors.

entries.question: How do the general's desert regiments feel about him favoring the Imperial ones?
entries.answer: The desert regiments resent it, and morale is low.

entries.question: How does the canyon city's general treat Alaric's Banner when they arrive?
entries.answer: He sees them as outsiders meddling in his command, and he ignores Alaric's warning that the enemy will come through the canyon.

entries.question: With the general ignoring him, what does Alaric do?
entries.answer: He wins over the desert regiment he is under, and slowly the other desert regiments.

entries.question: How does Alaric win the desert regiments over?
entries.answer: He treats them as equals (unlike the general), learns their ways and language, and wins them with his recon and intelligence.

entries.question: When the enemy hits the canyon, how does the battle start?
entries.answer: All three: Alaric's preparations hold the first wave; the general is caught off guard and the city nearly falls; the enemy uses spirit-tech or something nobody expected.

entries.question: What's the unexpected thing the enemy brings to the canyon?
entries.answer: Spirit-heavy creatures or fighters, and tunnels or a hidden route through the canyon.

entries.question: Who finds the tunnels or hidden route?
entries.answer: Seraphina's recon, and desert soldiers who know the canyon tell Alaric about it.

entries.question: How does the canyon battle end?
entries.answer: They hold the city, but the general takes the credit. It's a costly win with heavy losses.

entries.question: Who knows the truth that Alaric really saved the canyon city?
entries.answer: The desert regiments and Cassian. Rashid somewhat knows, but he needs to keep the armies united.

entries.question: What does Cassian do with what he knows about Alaric saving the canyon city?
entries.answer: Cassian praises Alaric privately, pulls Alaric closer as his protégé, and uses Alaric's win to push his own ideas.

entries.question: How does Seraphina react to her father pulling Alaric closer?
entries.answer: She's proud of Alaric and happy for him, and a little uneasy but can't say why yet.

entries.question: What happens to the general who took the credit for the canyon?
entries.answer: The general is promoted or rewarded.

entries.question: What does the canyon fight reveal about the spirit-heavy creatures or fighters?
entries.answer: They found out there are such things as spirit creatures and that they can be used.

entries.question: Who learns that spirit creatures can be used?
entries.answer: Only Alaric, Seraphina and their Banner learn it, plus Cassian, who learns it and connects it to the spirit-tech power he's chasing.

entries.question: Does Cassian tell them to keep the spirit creatures secret?
entries.answer: No, they keep it quiet on their own.
